claim: On October 30, 2023 AWS announced that you could request a limit increase through AWS Support so an on-demand stream scales up to 2 GB/s write and 4 GB/s read throughput. Earlier in the year the limit had been increased up to 1 GB/s write and 2GB/s read throughput.
question: How did the on-demand throughput limit of a Kinesis data stream change in 2023?

qualifiers.condition: increase requested through AWS Support; later superseded by the 10 GB/s limit of November 2024

claim: On Jul 24, 2026 Kinesis Data Streams added scale-down of ingest capacity with warm throughput. To scale down, set a lower warm throughput value on an on-demand stream, and the stream adjusts to the requested capacity or the amount needed to support peak data ingest usage in the last hour, whichever is higher. This is not examinable yet.

evidence.quote: To scale down, simply set a lower warm throughput value on your on-demand stream. The stream adjusts to the requested capacity or the amount needed to support peak data ingest usage in the last hour, whichever is higher.

note: NOT EXAMINABLE YET (GA after 2026-07-15). Current truth for the behavior is on the guide page how-do-i-size-a-stream (On-demand Advantage section).

claim: On Sep 23, 2026 Kinesis Data Streams started to support service-managed partition keys for On-Demand Standard and On-Demand Advantage streams, which distribute records across shards without requiring customers to specify partition keys. This suits workloads where record ordering is not required. It is not examinable yet.
question: Can a producer skip the partition key on Kinesis Data Streams, and what does it cost in ordering?

qualifiers.scope: On-Demand Standard and On-Demand Advantage streams
qualifiers.condition: for workloads where record ordering is not required; announced after 2026-07-15, so not examinable yet

evidence.quote: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now supports service-managed partition keys for On-Demand Standard and On-Demand Advantage streams, automatically distributing records across shards without requiring customers to specify partition keys to publish data. This capability simplifies data ingestion for workloads where record ordering is not required, eliminating hot partition keys and reducing time to production for streaming workloads.

evidence.heading: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams announces Service-Managed Partition Keys for simplified data ingestion

note: NOT EXAMINABLE YET (GA after 2026-07-15). Ordering per partition key still holds for streams that use partition keys; the service-managed strategy gives no ordering guarantee.
